network.overall_strategy: Use a convergent alpha-ketoglutarate-centered network in a single surface geothermal setting. Two C2 entry points feed glyoxylate (glycolate oxidation or glyoxal hydration-dehydrogenation), and three C3 entry points feed pyruvate (oxaloacetate decarboxylation, lactate oxidation, or acetaldehyde carboxylation). Glyoxylate and pyruvate then unite in the experimentally motivated pyruvate-glyoxylate condensation to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, which is converted by a net dehydration-hydrogenation step to alpha-ketoglutarate. Glutamate is reached by two alternative reductive aminations of alpha-ketoglutarate, using either H2 or formic acid/formate as the explicit reductant. Ten representative pathways are enumerated from these combinations.

reactions.name: Glycolate dehydrogenation to glyoxylate

conditions.other: anoxic geothermal mineral-interface pool; Fe2+-rich; mildly acidic to neutral

reactions.mechanism: Surface-assisted acceptorless dehydrogenation of an alpha-hydroxy acid to the corresponding aldehydo-acid.
reactions.reasoning: Oxidation of alpha-hydroxy acids to corresponding oxo or aldehydo acids is a recurring nonenzymatic transformation in iron-mediated prebiotic networks. Glycolate is therefore a chemically reasonable precursor to glyoxylate, and explicit H2 release keeps the redox bookkeeping conservative under anoxic mineral catalysis (Muchowska et al., 2019).

reactions.name: Glyoxal hydration-dehydrogenation to glyoxylate

conditions.other: anoxic geothermal pool; hydrated glyoxal adsorbed on sulfide surfaces

reactions.mechanism: Hydration of one aldehyde center followed by acceptorless dehydrogenation to the aldehydo-acid.
reactions.reasoning: Glyoxal is a plausible photochemical C2 dialdehyde. Conversion to glyoxylate by hydration plus dehydrogenation is chemically straightforward, although direct prebiotic demonstration under these exact conditions is limited. This route is therefore somewhat speculative, but it is atom-balanced and geochemically compatible with anoxic sulfide-rich surface pools.

reactions.name: Oxaloacetate decarboxylation to pyruvate

conditions.other: anoxic warm pool; oxaloacetate thermally labile

reactions.mechanism: Thermal decarboxylation of a labile oxaloacid to the corresponding alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Oxaloacetate is intrinsically decarboxylation-prone, and conversion to pyruvate plus CO2 is chemically facile without any need for molecular oxygen or a hidden redox partner. This is one of the cleaner nonenzymatic C4-to-C3 entries in the network.

reactions.name: Lactate dehydrogenation to pyruvate

conditions.other: anoxic mineral surface; H2 can diffuse away or be consumed downstream

reactions.mechanism: Metal-assisted dehydrogenation of a hydroxyacid to the corresponding ketoacid.
reactions.reasoning: Lactate and pyruvate form one of the simplest hydroxyacid/ketoacid redox pairs. A metal-mediated dehydrogenation route is therefore chemically conservative and keeps the reducing equivalent explicit as H2 rather than invoking an unstated oxidant (Muchowska et al., 2019).

reactions.name: Acetaldehyde carboxylation to pyruvate

conditions.other: CO2-rich, mildly alkaline mineral-interface pool; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Enolization of acetaldehyde followed by carboxylation to the alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Carboxylation of a reactive C2 carbonyl is a chemically economical entry to pyruvate. This step is less directly established than the pyruvate-glyoxylate condensation used later in the network, so it should be regarded as moderately speculative, but acetaldehyde is substantially more carboxylation-prone than acetate and the transformation is fully atom-balanced under CO2-rich mineral-interface conditions.

reactions.name: Glyoxylate-pyruvate condensation to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate

conditions.other: concentrated carbonyl pool at Fe2+-rich mineral interface; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Fe2+-mediated aldol-type addition of the pyruvate enol/enolate equivalent to glyoxylate.
reactions.reasoning: The pyruvate-glyoxylate union to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate is one of the best supported nonenzymatic entries into alpha-ketoglutarate-like chemistry. It provides a chemically coherent convergence of C2 and C3 feedstocks and is directly aligned with iron-promoted protometabolic networks (Muchowska et al., 2019).

reactions.name: Net dehydration-hydrogenation of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate to alpha-ketoglutarate
reactions.mechanism: Net sequence of beta-hydroxy-ketoacid dehydration to an unsaturated oxodicarboxylate followed by hydrogenation; represented as one balanced node.
reactions.reasoning: This reaction is written as the explicit net transformation from 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate to alpha-ketoglutarate with H2 as the reductant and H2O as coproduct. Mechanistically it corresponds to a short dehydration-plus-hydrogenation sequence rather than a single elementary event, but collapsing that sequence preserves atom balance while remaining consistent with Fe-mediated pyruvate-glyoxylate networks that access alpha-ketoglutarate (Muchowska et al., 2019).

reactions.name: H2-driven reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic NH3-rich pool with intermittent concentration at mineral interfaces

reactions.mechanism: Imine formation between alpha-ketoglutarate and ammonia followed by mineral-catalyzed hydrogenation.
reactions.reasoning: Alpha-ketoacids readily form imines with ammonia, and reduction of that imine gives the corresponding amino acid. A direct prebiotic demonstration for alpha-ketoglutarate to glutamate under exactly these conditions is limited, so this step should be treated as plausible but partly speculative; however, it is fully redox-explicit and chemically conservative.

reactions.name: Formate-driven reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.other: anoxic formate-rich mineral-interface pool; intermittent concentration favors imine formation

reactions.mechanism: Imine formation followed by transfer hydrogenation from formic acid/formate with decarboxylation.
reactions.reasoning: Formate is a plausible prebiotic reductant and transfer-hydrogen donor. Using formate instead of H2 supplies an alternative reductive amination route with explicit coproducts CO2 and H2O. This route is more speculative than the H2-driven version, but it is geochemically reasonable in formate-rich surface pools and keeps all redox accounting explicit.

pathways.name: Glycolate plus oxaloacetate via H2 amination
pathways.description: Glycolate is oxidized to glyoxylate, oxaloacetate decarboxylates to pyruvate, the C2 and C3 units condense to 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate, and H2 completes reductive amination to glutamate.

pathways.name: Glycolate plus oxaloacetate via formate amination
pathways.description: The same convergent carbon-skeleton route as P1, but the terminal amination is driven by formate rather than H2.

pathways.name: Glycolate plus lactate via H2 amination
pathways.description: Both branch feedstocks are hydroxy acids: glycolate and lactate are oxidized to glyoxylate and pyruvate before converging on alpha-ketoglutarate and glutamate.

pathways.name: Glycolate plus lactate via formate amination
pathways.description: The hydroxyacid-to-ketoacid branch pair is retained, but the terminal reduction of the alpha-keto acid uses formate as the hydrogen donor.

pathways.name: Glycolate plus acetaldehyde via H2 amination
pathways.description: A C2 oxidation route to glyoxylate is paired with aldehyde carboxylation to pyruvate, followed by the common alpha-ketoglutarate and glutamate steps.

pathways.name: Glyoxal plus oxaloacetate via H2 amination
pathways.description: Glyoxal is converted to glyoxylate while oxaloacetate supplies pyruvate; both feed the pyruvate-glyoxylate condensation before H2-driven amination.

pathways.name: Glyoxal plus oxaloacetate via formate amination
pathways.description: The glyoxal/oxaloacetate convergence route is retained, but glutamate formation is closed by formate-mediated reductive amination.

pathways.name: Glyoxal plus lactate via H2 amination
pathways.description: A photochemically plausible C2 dialdehyde entry and a hydroxyacid C3 entry converge through glyoxylate and pyruvate before mineral-mediated amination.

pathways.name: Glyoxal plus lactate via formate amination
pathways.description: The P8 skeleton-building route is coupled to formate-based terminal reduction, giving an alternative redox closure to glutamate.

pathways.name: Glyoxal plus acetaldehyde via formate amination
pathways.description: Both carbon branches begin from reactive C2 carbonyl compounds, converging through glyoxylate and pyruvate before the common alpha-ketoglutarate and glutamate steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Most convincing pathway in the set. Oxaloacetate decarboxylation and the pyruvate-glyoxylate condensation are strong, but glycolate dehydrogenation still needs an explicit catalytic surface and rxn_007 remains the main mechanistic uncertainty because the deoxygenation to alpha-ketoglutarate is compressed into a single net step.
suggestions: Specify mineral or metal surfaces and temperature/pH for rxn_001, rxn_007, and rxn_008.
Split rxn_007 into dehydration to an unsaturated C5 intermediate followed by hydrogenation.
Clarify the local source and fugacity of H2 in the surface setting.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Coherent and close to P1, but the final formate-driven reductive amination is more condition-sensitive because formate or formic acid speciation and the reduction mechanism are not defined. The same rxn_007 uncertainty remains.
suggestions: State whether rxn_009 is direct transfer hydrogenation or proceeds via formate decomposition to H2 and CO2.
Specify pH so NH3 availability and formate speciation are realistic.
Split rxn_007 into dehydration and reduction with explicit catalytic support.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Downstream logic is sound once pyruvate and glyoxylate are formed, but replacing oxaloacetate with lactate lowers confidence because lactate oxidation to pyruvate with H2 release is less secure under generic surface conditions. H2-driven amination is plausible if H2-activating minerals are present.
suggestions: Provide a catalyst or electron-transfer context for rxn_004 rather than leaving it as bare dehydrogenation.
Specify microenvironments that can support both oxidation steps and later H2-dependent reductions.
Add evidence or conditions for the rxn_007 deoxygenation sequence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route is coherent but stacks three medium-confidence steps: glycolate oxidation, lactate oxidation, and formate-driven reductive amination. The cumulative uncertainty makes it weaker than the oxaloacetate-based options.
suggestions: Define catalysts and pH for both dehydrogenations and the final amination.
Clarify whether formate reduces the imine directly or serves as a precursor to H2.
Provide an explicit intermediate sequence for rxn_007.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The central condensation chemistry is still reasonable, but the branch to pyruvate is weak because direct acetaldehyde carboxylation to pyruvate is mechanistically under-specified for a generic geothermal surface. That branch becomes the limiting step for the pathway.
suggestions: Replace rxn_005 with a better-supported multistep route to pyruvate or justify the carboxylation mechanism in detail.
Specify a mineral surface or activated CO2 chemistry if rxn_005 is retained.
Split rxn_007 into explicit dehydration and reduction substeps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest glyoxal-based route because oxaloacetate decarboxylation is robust and the downstream condensation is strong. Main concerns are glyoxal side reactivity, whether rxn_002 can selectively stop at glyoxylate under the stated surface conditions, and the under-specified rxn_007 deoxygenation.
suggestions: Address competing glyoxal hydration, oligomerization, and disproportionation pathways under the stated conditions.
Specify the catalytic surface for rxn_002 and how H2 evolution is achieved.
Provide an explicit intermediate and catalyst set for rxn_007.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically coherent, but both the glyoxal entry step and the formate-driven amination need tighter condition control than is currently stated. The route is plausible but less secure than P6 or P1.
suggestions: Define pH and mineral context so glyoxal handling and formate-based reduction are both realistic.
State whether rxn_009 is direct transfer hydrogenation or proceeds through H2 release from formate.
Split rxn_007 and cite or justify each substep.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway combines two moderate-risk oxidation steps before entering the stronger core condensation chemistry. It remains connected and balanced, but the cumulative need for selective dehydrogenation on a single surface setting lowers confidence.
suggestions: Provide catalysts or microenvironment separation for rxn_002 and rxn_004.
Address glyoxal side chemistry explicitly.
Support rxn_007 with an explicit dehydration intermediate and hydrogenation catalyst.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The route is logically complete, but it accumulates uncertainty at the entry stage and again in the final formate-driven amination. It is viable only if very specific catalytic and pH conditions are supplied.
suggestions: Specify catalysts and redox context for both oxidation steps.
Give a pH window that keeps enough free NH3 while also making formate-based reduction credible.
Decompose rxn_007 into explicit mechanistic substeps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Lowest-confidence pathway. It uses the weakest pyruvate entry step, a reactive glyoxal entry, and a condition-sensitive formate amination, so too many key transformations are under-specified even though the network remains formally balanced and connected.
suggestions: Replace or heavily justify rxn_005 with experimental support and a clear mechanism.
Address glyoxal stability and competing side reactions on the stated surface.
Provide explicit catalysts and conditions for rxn_007 and rxn_009.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is structurally valid: it is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and all 9 reactions pass the deterministic atom and charge balance check, so there are no conservation violations. The alpha-ketoglutarate-centered plan is coherent, and rxn_006 is the strongest chemistry because the pyruvate-glyoxylate condensation has good chemical precedent. Confidence is limited by several under-specified transformations, especially acceptorless oxidation to make glyoxylate or pyruvate with H2 release, the direct acetaldehyde plus CO2 to pyruvate step, and the compressed rxn_007 deoxygenation from 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate to alpha-ketoglutarate. A single surface geothermal setting could host the network only if local catalytic and redox microenvironments are available. Reductive amination to glutamate is plausible but needs explicit pH and mineral context, and reaction-specific literature support would strengthen the case. P1 is the best-supported pathway, but the network remains below the 0.9 approval threshold.
